feed.title: Randall Preserve's Five-Year First Phase to Include Wetlands, Visitor Center, and Trails
feed.summary: The initial five-year phase of restoration at the 387-acre Randall Preserve, supported by a $2 million state grant, will focus on wetlands restoration, constructing a new visitor center, and developing walking paths. Cleanup is expected to conclude by 2027, with public access anticipated to launch in approximately 18 months, or by 2028.

feed.title: Coastal Commission's 2016 Rejection of Banning Ranch Development Paved Way for Randall Preserve
feed.summary: Marking its 50th anniversary, the California Coastal Commission is highlighted for its critical 2016 decision to reject a large commercial development proposal on Newport Banning Ranch due to potential harm to wetlands and endangered species. The Commission's subsequent successful litigation ultimately led to the Trust for Public Lands acquiring the property in 2022 for permanent protection, establishing it as the Randall Preserve.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Kicks Off Five-Year First Phase of Restoration with $2M State Grant
feed.summary: The Randall Preserve has officially commenced its first phase of construction, testing, and cleanup, a project estimated to take approximately five years to complete. This initial phase, which includes wetlands restoration, the development of a visitor center, and walking paths, is being supported by a $2 million Proposition 4 grant. Assemblywoman Cottie Petrie-Norris presented the grant, highlighting the transformation of the former oil field into a protected coastal haven.
feed.source: Hoodline, Daily Pilot, LA Times, Supervisor Foley's Office

feed.title: Randall Preserve Hosts Community Open House Showcasing Progress and Future Plans
feed.summary: A community open house was held in Costa Mesa this month, attracting approximately two dozen attendees interested in the progress made at the Randall Preserve. Participants reviewed current developments and examined proposals for future trails and entrances. This event signifies ongoing public engagement as planning for the preserve's accessibility continues.

feed.title: Randall Preserve to Implement Dog and Bike Restrictions on Trails
feed.summary: Management plans for Randall Preserve indicate that public access will include specific restrictions, such as prohibiting dogs and bikes on the trails. Additionally, the 26 miles of dirt roads will be reduced to 5 miles of designated trails, with approximately 100 parking spaces near 17th Street.

feed.title: September 2026 Randall Preserve Newsletter Released
feed.summary: The Randall Preserve announced the release of its September 2026 newsletter via Instagram. The edition includes updates on upcoming plans for the preserve, a new Story Map feature, and a commemoration of the 10-year anniversary of the Coastal Commission Decision regarding the site.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Welcomes New Senior Community Organizer
feed.summary: Sergio Téllez has joined the Coastal Corridor Alliance (CCA) as a Senior Community Organizer. In this role, Téllez will focus on defending natural lands and empowering local communities to collaborate against harmful development, emphasizing grassroots efforts in conservation.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Trails Praised for Accessibility and Amenities
feed.summary: Recent tours of the Randall Preserve have highlighted its meticulously maintained and accessible trails, which were reportedly voted #1 in the nation last year. The preserve features amenities such as water fill stations, shaded rest areas, paved paths suitable for strollers, bathrooms, viewing windows for bogs, off-grid campsites, a stunning viewing deck, kids' play areas, picnic tables, and fishing ponds. These details offer a comprehensive look at the planned public access features.

feed.title: California Celebrates 50th Anniversary of Coastal Act
feed.summary: California marked the 50th anniversary of the landmark California Coastal Act, a visionary law instrumental in preserving vast coastal landscapes, including the former Newport Banning Ranch, now Randall Preserve. A celebration event was held on October 10th to honor the grassroots movement that led to its passage and its ongoing impact on coastal resource protection and the state's coastal economy.
feed.source: Facebook (Heal the Bay, California Coastal Commission, etc.)

feed.title: Green Heron Sighted Hunting at Randall Preserve
feed.summary: A recent social media post shared photographic evidence of a Green Heron successfully hunting a fish within the Randall Preserve. This sighting provides a tangible example of the preserve's active ecosystems and its role as a vital habitat for local wildlife.

feed.title: State Allocates Additional $2M for Randall Preserve Stewardship
feed.summary: Assemblywoman Cottie Petrie-Norris announced an additional $2 million in state funding for the Randall Preserve, secured through Prop. 4. These funds are designated for the preserve's stewardship and public access initiatives, a commitment also acknowledged by OC Supervisor Katrina Foley.
feed.source: Instagram/Facebook (Assemblywoman Cottie Petrie-Norris, OC Supervisor Katrina Foley)

feed.title: OCCF Contributes $200K to Randall Preserve for Endangered Species
feed.summary: Following a tour of Randall Preserve led by the Coastal Corridor Alliance, Orange County Community Foundation CEO Shelley Hoss announced a $200,000 contribution to an endowment fund dedicated to preserving endangered species on the site. The preserve is home to an estimated 45 rare or endangered species and 61 vernal pools, with initial public access expected by 2028.

feed.title: Randall Preserve to Open with Restricted Access, Reduced Trails
feed.summary: According to recent reports, Randall Preserve's extensive 26 miles of dirt roads will be significantly reduced to 5 miles of public trails. Initial public access, projected for 2028, will be limited to 10-person guided tours, and both dogs and bicycles will be prohibited.
feed.source: 南橙县新闻 (South Orange County News)

feed.title: Newport Beach Declares Emergency Amid Severe Coastal Flooding from Tropical Storm Rachel
feed.summary: Newport Beach declared a local emergency on October 9, 2026, as severe coastal flooding inundated streets on the Balboa Peninsula. High surf, elevated tides, and Tropical Storm Rachel caused significant damage, with flood warnings and advisories extending through October 13, impacting roads and some beachfront properties.

feed.title: Final Randall Preserve Management Plans Now Publicly Available Online
feed.summary: The final versions of the Randall Preserve's Resource Management Plan (RMP), Coastal Resilience Strategy (CRS), Public Access Plan (PAP), Recreation Impact Analysis (RIA), and Tribal Access and Engagement Plan (TAEP) have been published and are now available for public review. These comprehensive plans outline the future stewardship, public access, and ecological resilience of the preserve.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Hosts Donor Tour of Randall Preserve with OCCF
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance recently partnered with the Orange County Community Foundation to conduct a private tour for a select group of donors at the Randall Preserve. This engagement highlights ongoing efforts to involve stakeholders and secure funding for the preserve's development and conservation initiatives.

feed.title: Fidelity Associates Volunteer for Annual Coastal Cleanup Day
feed.summary: Fidelity associates from Irvine and Newport Beach participated in the annual Coastal Cleanup Day at Back Bay. Their efforts focused on removing litter, protecting local wildlife, and preserving Southern California's natural environments. The event also provided an opportunity for employees to connect while engaging in community service.

feed.title: Local News Outlet Solicits Public Input on Randall Preserve Features
feed.summary: JebSmithNews, a local news outlet, issued a call on social media for community members to provide feedback regarding the Randall Preserve. The request specifically invited input on desired features for the preserve, such as trails, wildlife restoration, and public access. This initiative aims to incorporate community perspectives into the future development of the preserve.

feed.title: Dedicated Website RandallPreserve.org Launched for Public Information
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance has announced the launch of RandallPreserve.org, a dedicated website offering comprehensive information on the newly established Randall Preserve. The site details the recently approved Resource Management Plan, Public Access Plan, Coastal Resilience Strategy, and Recreation Impact Analysis. This online resource will serve as a central hub for community engagement and updates.

feed.title: Randall Preserve to Feature 5 Miles of Trails and 100 Parking Spaces for Public Access
feed.summary: Management of the 387-acre Randall Preserve recently stated that the 26 miles of existing dirt roads will be converted into 5 miles of public trails. Additionally, approximately 100 parking spaces are planned near 17th Street to facilitate public access. Public entry will initially be limited to small guided groups of no more than 10 people, with restrictions on dogs and bikes.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Approves $2.4M Fundraising for Randall Preserve Projects
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance (CCA) Board of Directors has recently approved plans for a $2.4 million fundraising campaign. These funds are earmarked for various projects at the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve, including developing a unified visitor experience, planning for habitat restoration, creating a long-term vision plan, and establishing an interpretive center.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Anticipates Initial Public Access by Early 2027
feed.summary: Official information from the Randall Preserve indicates that an initial phase of public access is anticipated to be available no sooner than 2027. This update provides a slightly earlier target for public entry compared to previous projections of a partial public opening by 2028, aligning with the preserve's transformation into a nature park for passive recreation.

feed.title: Conservation Groups Continue Advocacy for Purchase of NMUSD Parcel Adjacent to Randall Preserve
feed.summary: The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) and the Randall Preserve are actively urging the Newport Mesa Unified School District (NMUSD) to sell or lease an 11.36-acre parcel adjacent to the preserve for permanent open-space protection. This ongoing advocacy aims to prevent development on the land, citing its irreplaceable coastal habitat and presence of sensitive species, to ensure the integrity of the preserve and public access to natural coastal space.

feed.title: OCCF Event Highlights Over 40 Acres Restored at Randall Preserve
feed.summary: The Orange County Community Foundation (OCCF) hosted its 'Protect & Preserve: A Look Inside the Randall Preserve' event on October 1, 2026, bringing together community leaders and environmental advocates. During the tour, it was highlighted that more than 40 acres of the 387.6-acre Randall Preserve have already been restored or are currently in the process of restoration, marking significant progress in its conservation. The event showcased ambitious plans to further restore the land, protect critical habitats, and connect the coastal corridor with surrounding parks and trails.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Anticipates Partial Public Opening by 2028 with Access Restrictions
feed.summary: The Randall Preserve, previously known as Banning Ranch, is expected to open to the public as early as 2028, with initial access limited to small guided tours of no more than 10 people. Management plans indicate that the existing 26 miles of dirt roads will be consolidated into 5 miles of designated trails, and public entry will prohibit dogs and cycling. Approximately 100 parking spaces are planned for installation near 17th Street.
feed.source: 南橙县新闻 (Southern Orange County News)

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance to Launch CorridorWatch Volunteer Program
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance (CCA) plans to design and implement a CorridorWatch Program in 2026-27. This initiative aims to establish a trained volunteer corps dedicated to monitoring, protecting, and stewarding sensitive coastal habitats, while also engaging with park visitors in public spaces. The program seeks to foster community trust and cross-cultural relationships through recurring collaboration, serving as visible park docents and habitat guardians.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Partners with Audubon Society for Monthly Bird Monitoring
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance, in partnership with the Sea and Sage Audubon Society, is conducting monthly bird monitoring activities at the Randall Preserve. These ongoing efforts have identified over 160 bird species utilizing the site, providing valuable data to track changes in bird populations over time.

feed.title: Community Bike Ride Celebrates 'Save Banning Ranch' Anniversary and Randall Preserve Plans
feed.summary: The City of Costa Mesa is hosting a community bike ride on September 13, 2026, to commemorate the 10-year anniversary of the 'Save Banning Ranch' decision. Participants will engage in an easy-paced 6-mile bike ride around the former Banning Ranch, now the Randall Preserve/Genga, to learn about its latest plans and share memories of the conservation efforts.

feed.title: MRCA Governing Board Formally Adopts Comprehensive Randall Preserve Management Plans
feed.summary: The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) Governing Board has formally adopted the complete Randall Preserve Property Management Plan package. This milestone, achieved after more than two years of collaborative planning, includes the Resource Management Plan, Public Access Plan, Coastal Resilience Strategy, and Recreation Impact Analysis, which together will guide habitat restoration, public access, recreation, and long-term stewardship of the 387-acre preserve. The Public Access Plan outlines more than five miles of trails planned on the Preserve.
feed.source: California Native Plant Society (CNPS Chapters) / Orange County Conservation & Advocacy Update, Coastal Corridor Alliance

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Secures Grant for Wetland and Vernal Pool Studies
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance has received a grant from the State Coastal Conservancy in 2026 to fund studies on restoring tidal wetlands and analyzing vernal pools within the Randall Preserve. This initiative involves hiring Moffatt & Nichol to explore restoration alternatives and assess vernal pools for the federally listed San Diego Fairy Shrimp, particularly with the anticipated 2026-27 El Niño season.

feed.title: Trust for Public Land Closes Escrow on Banning Ranch, Securing Randall Preserve as Public Park
feed.summary: The Trust for Public Land has successfully closed escrow on the Banning Ranch property, now officially known as the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve. This milestone, achieved after two decades of dedicated preservation efforts, permanently protects 387 acres of coastal Orange County land and designates it as a public park to be managed by the Mountains Recreation & Conservation Authority (MRCA).

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Highlights Shorebird Protection Challenges in Newport Beach
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance has published an article detailing the challenges faced by shorebirds like the threatened Western Snowy Plover and federally endangered California Least Tern in the Coastal Corridor. The article specifically notes the impact of dog presence on nesting sites, contrasting Huntington State Beach's 'No Dogs' policy with Newport Beach's allowance of dogs during certain hours, which contributes to habitat loss and reduced nesting for these sensitive species.

feed.title: Documentary Highlights Significant Funding for Randall Preserve Acquisition and Environmental Mitigation
feed.summary: A new documentary, 'Protect & Preserve: Orange County's Unique Ecosystems,' has brought to light the substantial financial investment that facilitated the creation of the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve. This included a $97 million acquisition and a comprehensive $243.5 million environmental mitigation program, effectively transforming a former oil field into protected public land.

feed.title: Wetland Restoration Feasibility Study Kicked Off for Randall Preserve
feed.summary: The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) and Coastal Corridor Alliance announced the official kick-off of a Wetland Restoration Feasibility Study for the Randall Preserve. This study aims to explore opportunities for creating new coastal wetlands in areas that have been historically diked, identifying possibilities and constraints for future restoration efforts.
feed.source: Randall Preserve Press Release / Coastal Corridor Alliance

feed.title: OCCF to Host 'Protect & Preserve: A Look Inside the Randall Preserve' Event
feed.summary: The Orange County Community Foundation (OCCF) is scheduled to host an event titled 'Protect & Preserve: A Look Inside the Randall Preserve' on September 25, 2026. This event, which aims to provide insights into the preserve, will run from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM.

feed.title: Encampment Cleared at Randall Preserve
feed.summary: On August 7, 2026, an encampment at the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve, formerly Banning Ranch, was cleared through a multi-agency effort. Agencies involved included the Newport Beach City crew, USACE cleanup crews and Park Rangers, Newport Beach Police Department, Orange County Sheriff's Department, CMPD Park Rangers, and outreach workers. Eviction notices were reportedly posted prior to the cleanup, with approximately three individuals contacted during the operation.

feed.title: Federal Government Initiates Review of California's Coastal Management Program
feed.summary: The federal government has initiated a review of California's Coastal Management Program, with concerns raised by organizations like the Coastal Corridor Alliance that the goal is decertification, potentially threatening the state's coastal protection efforts. The California Coastal Commission, currently celebrating 50 years of the Coastal Act, emphasized its success in preserving areas such as Newport Banning Ranch and its contribution to a significant coastal economy. Public input is being sought to support California's coastal laws.
feed.source: Coastal Corridor Alliance (Facebook), California Coastal Commission (Facebook)

feed.title: Orange County Community Foundation's Warne Fund Supports Randall Preserve Conservation
feed.summary: The Orange County Community Foundation (OCCF) Warne Family Endowment Fund has significantly contributed to the Randall Preserve's conservation, providing $165,000 over five years for advocacy and mobilizing over $135 million in additional funding. This support has been crucial for protecting endangered species within the preserve, formerly known as Banning Ranch.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Planning Documents Reach Draft Final Stage
feed.summary: Several key planning documents for the Randall Preserve, including the Resource Management Plan, Coastal Resilience Strategy, Public Access Plan, Recreation Impact Analysis, and the adopted Tribal Access and Engagement Plan, have advanced to their 'Draft Final' stage. This indicates significant progress in outlining the future restoration, protection, and low-impact public access for the preserve. Melanie Schlotterbeck, Stewardship Consultant for the Coastal Corridor Alliance, is noted for her role in advancing these crucial documents.
feed.source: Facebook (California Seabreeze Community, Coastal Corridor Alliance)

feed.title: Coastal Commission to Consider Reduced Banning Ranch Development Amidst Land Trust Concerns
feed.summary: The Coastal Commission is scheduled to meet on September 7th to review a development proposal for Banning Ranch, with staff recommending a reduction from approximately 50 acres to 20 acres, and a decrease in dwelling units from 900 to around 500. This meeting will also address ongoing concerns regarding the Newport Banning Land Trust's board, which critics allege lacks conservation expertise and has ties to real estate developers.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Featured in New PBS Documentary on Orange County Ecosystems
feed.summary: The Frank and Joan Randall Preserve was spotlighted in the new episode of 'The Power of Community' titled 'Protect & Preserve: Orange County's Unique Ecosystems,' which premiered on Monday, August 31, 2026, at 5 p.m. on KLCS/PBS. The documentary, sponsored by the Orange County Community Foundation, highlights the preserve's vital role in wetland restoration, its importance as a habitat for endangered wildlife, and its provision of natural open space for the community, showcasing the transformation of a former oil field into protected land.
feed.source: KLCS/PBS, Orange County Community Foundation (via Facebook), Coastal Corridor Alliance

feed.title: NMUSD Implements E-Bike Ban for K-8 Students Starting 2026-2027 School Year
feed.summary: The Newport-Mesa Unified School District (NMUSD) has officially approved a policy banning e-bikes for all students in kindergarten through 8th grade, effective for the 2026-2027 school year. This decision follows growing safety concerns and discussions regarding student transportation to school.

feed.title: Huntington Beach Airshow Permit Lacks Altitude Restrictions Over Randall Preserve
feed.summary: Concerns have been raised that the California Coastal Commission's Coastal Development Permit for the Huntington Beach Airshow, approved in August 2025, does not include altitude restrictions for aircraft flying over the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve. This omission differs from protections for other ecological reserves and highlights potential impacts on the preserve's wildlife and air quality.

feed.title: MRCA Conducts Site Visit to Randall Preserve for Remediation Review
feed.summary: The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority's Park Development and Watershed Planning team recently visited the Randall Preserve to review the ongoing remediation efforts being conducted by the former owners, as part of assessing future improvements for the preserve.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance and MRCA Engage in Outreach and Fire Prevention Efforts
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance and the Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority are reportedly conducting significant outreach efforts and collaborating with the City and County of Newport Beach on fire prevention initiatives during the ongoing land remediation at the Randall Preserve.

feed.title: NMUSD Parcel Negotiations Continue, Stormwater Concerns Raised for Randall Preserve
feed.summary: Negotiations persist for an 11-acre Newport-Mesa Unified School District parcel bordering the Randall Preserve, with a developer proposing housing units amidst calls for its preservation as open space. Additionally, the Coastal Corridor Alliance and MRCA have expressed concerns regarding the City's potential discharge of untreated storm drain water onto the Randall Preserve as part of a separate Fairview Developmental Center plan.

feed.title: NMUSD Parcel Public Review Period Concludes, Nears Final Process
feed.summary: Following a 30-day public review period, the Newport-Mesa Unified School District (NMUSD) parcel adjacent to the Randall Preserve is now moving towards a final public process as mandated by the County. This next phase will determine the future of the 11-acre site, which has been subject to competing proposals for development versus preservation as open space.

feed.title: Newport Beach City Council Debates 16th Street Entrance to Randall Preserve
feed.summary: During a recent City Council discussion, concerns were raised regarding a potential primary entrance to the Randall Preserve off West 16th Street, adjacent to a new development. Some council members advised the applicant to reconsider lighting for the nearby project, noting that the 17th Street entrance is considered more suitable for the preserve.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance to Host Outreach Meeting on Randall Preserve's Future
feed.summary: David Martinez announced that the Coastal Corridor Alliance will hold an outreach meeting to discuss documents pertaining to the future use of the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve/Genga. This event aims to engage the community on the ongoing planning for the preserve.

feed.title: ExxonMobil Proposes Large-Scale Development on Banning Ranch
feed.summary: ExxonMobil, the owner of Banning Ranch, has proposed a large-scale development plan for 212 acres of the site, including nearly 1,400 condos, homes, a hotel, and retail space. This proposal represents a significant threat to the conservation efforts for the area.
feed.source: Facebook (Protecting Banning, CA's environment for wildlife and residents)

feed.title: Concerns Raised Over Newport Banning Land Trust Board's Conservation Expertise
feed.summary: A recent online discussion highlighted concerns regarding the Newport Banning Land Trust's board members, alleging a lack of conservation background and potential ties to real estate developers. The critique suggests that the Trust's stated mission to steward natural land and native species may be compromised by the board's composition.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Continues Monthly Beach Cleanups at Santa Ana River Mouth
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance is continuing its regular beach cleanup efforts, held on the fourth Saturday of every month at Newport Lifeguard Tower 74, located at the Santa Ana River Mouth. These cleanups aim to remove trash and protect the local waterways and wildlife.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Hosts Monthly Native Gardening at Fairview Park
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance, in collaboration with the City of Costa Mesa, is regularly hosting native gardening events at Fairview Park. These efforts, held on the third Saturday of each month, involve volunteers in removing invasive plants, collecting and planting native species, and maintaining the park's natural habitats.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Proximity Highlights Local Real Estate Value
feed.summary: Recent real estate activity in Newport Beach, observed over the last 30 days, indicates that properties, particularly in the Newport Crest community, adjacent to or overlooking the Randall Preserve are being marketed with an emphasis on their proximity to the designated open space. These listings leverage the preserve's scenic views and natural surroundings as a significant amenity, reflecting a positive impact on local property appeal and desirability.
feed.source: Local Real Estate Listings / Rentable / MLS Listings

feed.title: Debate Continues Over 11-Acre NMUSD Parcel Adjacent to Randall Preserve
feed.summary: Negotiations are ongoing for an 11-acre parcel owned by the Newport-Mesa Unified School District (NMUSD) adjacent to the Randall Preserve, with competing proposals for its future. A developer is bidding to lease the land for nearly 200 housing units, while community advocates, including the Coastal Corridor Alliance, are pushing for its preservation as public open space, integrated with the nature preserve.
feed.source: OC Register (via Coastal Corridor Alliance Facebook) / Hoodline / Los Angeles Times / Facebook

feed.title: Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy Offers $2.0M Grant for Randall Preserve
feed.summary: The Santa Monica Mountains Conservancy has an open grant, 'Prop 4 – Randall Preserve,' offering $2.0 million for projects supporting the reduction of climate impacts on disadvantaged communities and the creation or expansion of outdoor recreation opportunities within the Randall Preserve. These funds are available for encumbrance or expenditure until June 30, 2028.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Announces September Beach & River Mouth Cleanup
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance has announced a 'Special Beach Cleanup | Especial Limpieza de Playa' scheduled for Saturday, September 19, 2026. Volunteers are invited to participate at Newport Lifeguard Tower 74, located at the Santa Ana River Mouth, to help clean and restore the coastal corridor's habitats and protect local wildlife.

feed.title: Randall Preserve Property Management Plan Formally Adopted by MRCA Governing Board
feed.summary: The Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) Governing Board has formally adopted the Randall Preserve Property Management Plan. This comprehensive plan outlines the future stewardship of the preserve, including the development of over five miles of trails that will offer scenic views of Catalina Island, Mt. Baldy, and the Palos Verdes Peninsula.

feed.title: Melanie Schlotterbeck Credited for Advancing Randall Preserve Planning Documents
feed.summary: Melanie Schlotterbeck, Stewardship Consultant for the Coastal Corridor Alliance, has been specifically credited this month with significantly advancing two core planning documents for the Randall Preserve. Her two decades of conservation experience were highlighted as crucial for bringing these important documents to completion.

feed.title: Coastal Corridor Alliance Publishes August 2026 Randall Preserve Newsletter
feed.summary: The Coastal Corridor Alliance has released its August 2026 Randall Preserve newsletter, providing updates on the final Randall Preserve plans, including details from the press release regarding the plans and acknowledging major contributors to their development.

timeline.title: Land Acquired
timeline.description: 387 acres on the Newport Beach coast — the Frank and Joan Randall Preserve (formerly Banning Ranch) — protected through a $50 million private gift; title held by the MRCA.

timeline.title: Oil Operations Wind Down
timeline.description: Active oil production ends; environmental assessment and remediation planning begin across the former oil field.

timeline.title: Oil Well Remediation
timeline.description: More than 300 former oil wells are being capped and abandoned to environmental standards — the largest phase of cleanup, running through 2027.

timeline.title: Habitat & Resource Planning
timeline.description: Resource management and restoration plans developed to guide the return of native coastal sage scrub, wetlands, and bluff habitats.

timeline.title: Recreation & Open Space Plan (Draft)
timeline.description: Draft plan proposes roughly 7 miles of public trails, gateways, and interpretive areas — currently under review.

timeline.title: Boundary Parcel Negotiations
timeline.description: MRCA and Newport-Mesa Unified School District enter negotiations over an 11.36-acre parcel inside the preserve boundary.

timeline.title: Remediation Target
timeline.description: Targeted completion of oil-well capping and major site cleanup.

timeline.title: Public Access Opens
timeline.description: Phased opening of trails, gateways, and restored coastal habitat to the public.

neighborWatch.title: Boundary Fire Safety
neighborWatch.description: The preserve sits in a High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. During remediation the site operator (Aera Energy) clears brush only twice a year; residents along the eastern edge have flagged flashy-fuel buildup and illegal encampments as ignition risks.

neighborWatch.title: Firebreak Pathway Proposal
neighborWatch.description: A proposal under discussion would add a permanent multi-use pathway along the 17th–19th Street boundary — serving as both a firebreak and an emergency-access route for fire crews.

neighborWatch.title: AB 1203 — Coastal Land Protection
neighborWatch.description: State bill touching coastal land protection; a committee hearing was postponed to the summer 2026 session. Public input matters most at the hearing stage.

neighborWatch.title: NMUSD Parcel Negotiations
neighborWatch.description: Newport-Mesa school board is in closed-session negotiations with the MRCA over the 11.36-acre parcel inside the preserve boundary (since May 19, 2026).

neighborWatch.title: Trail Status
neighborWatch.description: Public trails remain under development; official access is expected in 2027 or later. Please respect posted closures and boundaries.
